claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
In-flight pre-heating of the feedstock to 250–300°C will enhance particle melting.
Enhanced particle melting will improve splat formation.
Plasma pre-heating will produce a coating thickness exceeding the stated 15–45 μm baseline.
Plasma pre-heating under the proposed conditions will keep as-sprayed oxidation minimal.
Pre-heating will increase the molten fraction and fluidity of particles at impact.
Greater molten fraction and fluidity will improve splat flattening.
Greater molten fraction and fluidity will improve inter-splat bonding.
Pre-heating reduces the additional in-flight energy required for complete particle melting.
Reduced melting-energy demand produces a more uniform molten state at impact.
Avoiding excessive energy input minimizes thermal gradients.
Minimized thermal gradients reduce oxidation during spraying.
The proposed treatment will preserve coating microstructural integrity.
The resulting coating will provide robust performance in high-temperature thermal-barrier-coating service.
Spraying the 15–45 μm feedstock without pre-heating produces insufficient coating thickness.
The intervention remains effective only when the pre-heating temperature is maintained within 250–300°C in a controlled inert atmosphere.
Exceeding 300°C may increase oxidation or cause unwanted phase changes.
Departing from controlled atmospheric conditions may increase oxidation or cause unwanted phase changes.

contradictions.description: The 15–45 μm value is initially identified as the feedstock particle-size range, but elsewhere it is treated as a baseline coating-thickness range. This conflates powder size with deposited coating thickness and makes the predicted thickness comparison and falsification threshold internally inconsistent.
